title: Abstracts 4
program_note:
Abstracts 4 is based upon music drawn from Abstracts 2 and Abstracts 3.  It was inspired by manhole covers in city streets (in this case, in Moscow and New York City), some abstractly, some more directly pictorially. In “Twelve-Bar Benzenes,” the arrangement of hexagons — benzene rings? — in circles of twelve brought to mind both The Blues and other numerically-regular cycles of phrases and pitches. “Neural Net” made me think of a network of multiple linear connections.  The repeated, simple pattern in “Balance Bars,” both heavy and block-like and yet light, inspired an idea of short melodic lines moving in parallel (and yet—not).  Lastly, “Tetrominoes” reminded me of the old video game Tetris, with the way its pieces fit together, along with the Eastern European melodies—except that Klezmer tunes are substituted for the original Russian melodies.
Abstracts 4 is about 16’20” total duration, with the individual movements approximately as shown:
1.  Twelve-Bar Benzenes (3’50”) (attacca)
2.  Neural Net (2’40”)
iii. Balance Bars (4’15”)
iii. Tetrominoes (5’35”)
David S. Lefkowitz
Los Angeles, CA
14 April, 2019
